liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **When Push Comes To Shove** (1 review): One of the finest versions, preventing the first set from dragging [25]
- **Desolation Row** (1 review): Jerry's fills and harmonies make the song lilt nimbly instead of plodding [18]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): The performance sends the listener into another world, escaping into the next realm [18]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Jerry's sustain and slight distortion at the solo peak are subtle beauty [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-03-26.138166.sbd.miller.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 149 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: The low end on this recording is described as absolutely thunderous [1]
- **gd1987-03-26.145505.ots.at835b.akg.d12e.blend.ackerman.noel.t-flac16**: audience recording; 20 songs; 144 min [3]
- **gd1987-03-26.nakcm304.suraci.81450.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 146 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [5]. Said about its sound: Very beginning of Midnight Hour is clipped, and tape flip occurs during Desolation Row [5]
- **gd87-03-26.mixed.braverman.10923.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 140 min; rated 4.36/5 by 38 [13]. Said about its sound: First set tracking speed is too fast, making it nearly unlistenable; Second set has normal pitch and a good audience/soundboard mix; Recording has always felt like a soundboard, though muddled in some areas [16][24][26]

## Around the show

- Reviewer entered with a wrong ticket, describing the night as magical [17]
- Reviewer calls the venue good but criticizes the recording quality heavily [21]
- Jerry was clearly bounced back from his coma, playing tight with high energy [23]
- The 1987 Hartford shows were referred to as the ‘tea-hee fest’ [3]
- Spring 1987 tour was the strongest since Summer 1985, harkening back to 1982 [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-03-26.138166.sbd.miller.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Ultra Matrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90) [1]
- **gd1987-03-26.145505.ots.at835b.akg.d12e.blend.ackerman.noel.t-flac16**: taped by Ray Ackerman; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: Ray Ackerman’s Master Audience Cassettes; Two x Audio Technica 835b + One x AKG D12e center fill > Realistic 32-1105A, 4 channel stereo mixer > Sony TCD5 (OTS) [3]. Also: Edited and mastered by Joe Noel from 24/96 WAV to 16-bit FLAC [3]
- **gd1987-03-26.nakcm304.suraci.81450.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Tony Suraci; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: Nak CM304's>Sony D5 [5]
- **gd87-03-26.mixed.braverman.10923.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD [13]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by RareVinyl.com: [Grateful Dead Dave's Picks Volume 36: Hartford Civic Center, Hartford, CT 3/26/87 & 3/27/87 - Sealed 2020 US 4-CD set](https://us.rarevinyl.com/products/grateful-dead-dave-s-picks-volume-36-hartford-civic-center-hartford-ct-3-26-87-and-3-27-87-sealed-us-4-cd-album-set-r2607319-866381) [29]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1987-03-26 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1987-03-26-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [30]
- Fan art by Jake May: [Grateful Dead Prep 3/26/87 and 3/27/87 Shows in Hartford for Archival 'Dave's Picks' Release](https://jambands.com/news/2020/10/15/grateful-dead-prep-3-36-87-and-3-37-87-shows-in-hartford-for-archival-daves-picks-release/) [31]
